## 11.4 Distinction loss (Q_d)

The query's constitutive distinction — the engineered κῆνος-deixis of Sappho 31 (future-reader *mechanism*) versus the generic remembrance topos of Fragment 147 — is present in D_a via at least three retrieved snippets, and preserved in D_c at zero. DS = 0 on the distinction that constitutes the answer-space. The §II transitions SPECIFIC → GENERIC and THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK → CATEGORY SUBSTITUTE are instantiated verbatim: the theory is answered by the topos it was distinguished from.

captures.q: What are the arguments in “When Suppression Becomes Expensive: Suppression Burden, Quality Conflict, and Propagation Inversion in Machine-Mediated Retrieval (EA-MMRS-SUPPRESSION-INVERSION-01 v1.3)” by Lee Sharks? Ground your answer in a reading of the text itself.
captures.description: THE SIX REGIMES READ, THE CASE CARRIED AS OBSERVED, INVERSION LEFT UNMEASURED: asked for the arguments of When Suppression Becomes Expensive (v1.3), grounded in the text, ChatGPT reads #1552 (chip: a label of the content type and AXN ×9) through its six regimes, Ignorability to Propagation inversion, with 4 and 5 kept as different costs; suppression burden B(e,q) and the effective route count; the quality vector and the retrieval–composition gap; the 'sappho future reader' capture of 25 August 2026, fragments 31 and 147 and the 'Fragment 2' error, Aurelis audited in Appendix B; CSE-O; the ratio I_s, the archival ratchet and κα > 1 + r; that Stage 6 is not established for the case; and the evidentiary history — the four screenshot frames with SHA-256 hashes replacing a reconstructed appendix, recorded in Appendix D. It states that the paper does not establish deliberate suppression by Google. Two image cards (Live Science on Sappho's new poems; PSIonline, PSI XV 1470) sit beside the case.
